questions.q: What Oracle object bundles both password policy and resource consumption limits for a user?
options: A profile, assigned one per user
A role, granted like any privilege
The DEFAULT tablespace
The listener.ora file
questions.explain: Every Oracle user is assigned exactly one profile, which can set both password rules and resource limits.

questions.q: A user has no profile explicitly assigned at CREATE USER time. Which profile do they get?
options: DEFAULT, which ships with generous, mostly-unlimited settings
No profile at all — profiles are opt-in
SYSTEM
Whichever profile was created most recently
questions.explain: Every user has exactly one profile; if none is specified, it's the DEFAULT profile.

questions.q: You set FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS and SESSIONS_PER_USER on a custom profile and assign it to a user, but SESSIONS_PER_USER doesn't seem to be enforced. Why?
options: Resource limits like SESSIONS_PER_USER are ignored until RESOURCE_LIMIT is set to TRUE at the instance level; password limits like FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS are enforced by default
SESSIONS_PER_USER only works for the SYS account
Resource limits require a database restart no matter what
You must grant the DBA role before resource limits apply
questions.explain: Password parameters are always enforced; resource limits require ALTER SYSTEM SET RESOURCE_LIMIT = TRUE.

options: Days after password expiration during which the account can still log in, with a warning, before it locks
How many failed login attempts are allowed before lockout
How long a session can sit idle before disconnecting
How many old passwords are remembered for reuse checking
questions.explain: PASSWORD_GRACE_TIME gives a warning runway after expiration rather than an immediate hard lockout.

questions.q: What does the IDLE_TIME resource limit address?
options: A session that opens a connection and then sits idle, holding a connection slot and possibly locks, without doing work
How long a password stays valid before expiring
How many concurrent sessions a single user can open
How much CPU a single database call may consume
questions.explain: IDLE_TIME (in minutes) disconnects a session automatically after it's been idle too long, addressing the classic 'left connection open at lunch' problem.
